quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Always ride in the same spot in the lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on the road and traffic around you.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Yellow
Blue
White
Red

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean the opposite way from the motorcycle and turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When traffic is light.
When traffic is heavy.
When you can see the road through vehicles ahead.
When the weather is pleasant and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when traffic is heavy, at night, in bad weather, or when you cannot see ahead clearly. A two-second distance is generally adequate in good conditions.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group ride?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Just behind the lead rider.
At the back of the group.
Anywhere in the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit the distance you travel each day.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Ride no more than about six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may become extremely tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when the front brake is used.
Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
Applies equal braking to both wheels when either brake is used.
Remembers the braking force you typically use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever the rear brake is used. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your braking system.

questions.question: How do you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Turn the handlebars quickly.
Shift your weight quickly.
Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn.
Press the handgrip on the opposite side of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn.
questions.explanation: Apply pressure to the handgrip on the side you want to go. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: What is the correct way to swerve?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn.
Press the handgrip on the opposite side of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip on the side of your desired turn. Then press the opposite handgrip to straighten out once you are clear of the hazard.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection on a motorcycle?

options.text: No, a helmet is enough.
Yes, in addition to a helmet.
Only on windy days.
No, not if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing even with a helmet. Hearing protection helps prevent this while letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: How often must a motorcycle pass a safety inspection?

options.text: Once a year
Once every two years
Once every four years
Once every five years

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a year
questions.explanation: All motorcycles registered in Utah must pass a safety inspection every year. Some areas also require an emissions test.

questions.question: When the road is wet, which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
All areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Oil drippings from cars collect in the center of the lane. This area loses traction when wet. You can ride to the side and still stay in your lane.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, drivers can see you easily.
No, drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
No, it is illegal to ride outside the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: Small vehicles like motorcycles can appear ______ and seem to travel ______ than they actually do.

options.text: farther away, more slowly
farther away, faster
closer, more slowly
closer, faster

questions.correctAnswerText: farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may look farther away and slower than they actually are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their real location and speed.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you turn?

options.text: Just your head.
Your head and shoulders.
Just your shoulders.
Your entire body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Speed up.
Follow closer to the vehicle ahead.
Use the headlights of the vehicle ahead to help you see.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of the vehicle ahead to help you see.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Behind the operator.
Anywhere, they do not need to reach the footrests.
Holding onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front may not balance properly and could block your controls.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do to stay safe at night when other drivers have trouble seeing them?

options.text: Reduce their speed.
Sound the horn repeatedly.
Not ride at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle so its headlights shine on you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the lights of vehicles ahead to help you see. Use your high beam headlight when safe, and be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: When going through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay in the left part of the lane.
Always stay in the right part of the lane.
Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to move to a different lane position when needed. The best path through a curve does not always match the curve of the road.

questions.question: What is true about the center of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best place for a motorcycle.
It often has oil and grease, but is usually safe.
It often has oil and grease, and is never safe.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often has oil and grease, but is usually safe.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of each lane. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. Avoid large buildups of oil and grease, which are common at busy intersections and toll booths.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center part of the lane.
In the left part of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.
In any part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center part of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This discourages the other driver from returning to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When a vehicle tries to pass you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the center part of the lane.
Move to the left part of the lane.
Move to the right part of the lane.
Do not worry about which part of the lane you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center part of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, what should you do?

options.text: Always ride in the center part of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.
Always ride in the right part of the lane.
Be flexible and consider many factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible and consider many factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. You do not need to avoid any part of the lane all the time. Choose the position where drivers can see you best and where you have space around you.
